header.subject: Science
header.title: Activity 3.4: role of decomposers
header.goal: Children say what bacteria and fungi break down.

card.bring: textbook p.47 · leaf, roti, wrapper · books, pencils

moves.do: Open p.47; the class says the recall answers together.
moves.how: Energy comes from the … → Sun. A rabbit gets about … → 10%.
moves.say: “At home, where do old leaves and bread go?”

moves.do: Read the leaves story; See, Think, Wonder, p.47.
moves.how: Leaves fall, yet the ground stays clear. Class: “I see…”.
moves.say: “Where do all the fallen leaves go?”

moves.think: The leaf is dead, so decomposers feed on it. I predict it turns thin and crumbly. I write: will break down.
moves.do: Draw leaf, bacteria dots and mushroom; predict the leaf.
moves.how: Say the six key words with Urdu. Draw the arrows.
moves.say: “The leaf does not vanish: bacteria and fungi break it down.”

moves.do: Bury leaf, roti, wrapper; class writes a prediction for each.
moves.how: Copy the table; wash hands after.
moves.say: “Roti in damp soil: bacteria and fungi will …” → “break it down.”

turn.a: Roti in damp soil: what will happen to it?
turn.b: Fungi break it down, it was alive. Plastic wrapper?
turn.help: Point to p.47; read the line.

moves.do: One minute: ask your neighbour about roti or the wrapper.
moves.how: Zainab and Bilal show first. Check five books.
1 blanks · 2 two kinds · 3 Zainab's log · 4 no decomposers · 5 home. Done? Dead cow.

answers: Dead matter piles up; no mineral salts
sections.mistake: Says the Sun dried it. Ask: “Who breaks it down?”
sections.stuck: Give the board picture with the three words written.

moves.do: Say: “A fish dies; a steel spoon lies in damp soil. Which rots?”

sections.correct: The fish; the spoon was never alive.
sections.success: I can say what bacteria and fungi break down and why.
sections.ask: Why do bacteria and fungi leave the spoon alone?
sections.listen: Never alive: decomposers break down only dead or waste matter.

moves.do: Look at the buried cups after one week.
moves.how: Write one sentence on what changed in each.

expect.html:
GRADE 5 · SCIENCE · Ch.3 EcosystemDay 7 · 40 min

Activity 3.4: role of decomposers

Children say what bacteria and fungi break down.
Bringtextbook p.47 · leaf, roti, wrapper · books, pencils Wordsdecomposer · تحلیل کار · bacteria · جراثیم · fungi · پھپھوندی · microorganism · خوردبینی جاندار · mineral salts · معدنی نمکیات · decompose · گلنا سڑنا
PRACTICE · 25 of 40 min
4′ 8′ 12′ 13′ 3′
OpenExplainWe DoYou Do✓
★ Your one thing today · in move

Opening

0–4′Full details ›
1

Open p.47; the class says the recall answers together. Energy comes from the … → Sun. A rabbit gets about … → 10%. “At home, where do old leaves and bread go?”

2

Read the leaves story; See, Think, Wonder, p.47. Leaves fall, yet the ground stays clear. Class: “I see…”. “Where do all the fallen leaves go?”

Explanation · I Do

4–12′Full details ›
3

Draw leaf, bacteria dots and mushroom; predict the leaf. Say the six key words with Urdu. Draw the arrows. “The leaf does not vanish: bacteria and fungi break it down.”Think aloud: “The leaf is dead, so decomposers feed on it. I predict it turns thin and crumbly. I write: will break down.”

We Do

12–24′Full details ›
4

I START, YOU FINISH
Bury leaf, roti, wrapper; class writes a prediction for each. Copy the table; wash hands after. “Roti in damp soil: bacteria and fungi will …” → “break it down.”

5

ONE NEIGHBOUR TURN
One minute: ask your neighbour about roti or the wrapper. Zainab and Bilal show first. Check five books. “Roti row, wrapper row, then swap.”Window side first: “Roti in damp soil: what will happen to it?” → Reply: “Fungi break it down, it was alive. Plastic wrapper?” · Stop: two claps · Stuck? Point to p.47; read the line.

You Do · in the book

24–37′Full details ›
6

⏱ 24′ stop explaining
Write 'Decomposers'; do items 1-5 alone. 1 blanks · 2 two kinds · 3 Zainab's log · 4 no decomposers · 5 home. Done? Dead cow. “Item 4: two sentences.”If stuck: Give the board picture with the three words written.

Check 5 books · answers

1.mineral salts, carbon dioxide, water
2.bacteria and fungi
3.Fungi break the log down
4.Dead matter piles up; no mineral salts
5.Roti gets mouldy: a fungus

Likely mistake

Says the Sun dried it. Ask: “Who breaks it down?”

THE BOARD BY THE END · Dead leaf to three simple things

Check · exit ticket

37–40′Full details ›
7

Say: “A fish dies; a steel spoon lies in damp soil. Which rots?” Five answer alone, aloud. Then: “Why?” “Thumbs first, then answer.”Ask: “Why do bacteria and fungi leave the spoon alone?” → Listen for: Never alive: decomposers break down only dead or waste matter.Success: “I can say what bacteria and fungi break down and why.” 👍 or ✊ firstCorrect: The fish; the spoon was never alive.

Homework

at homeFull details ›
8

Look at the buried cups after one week. Write one sentence on what changed in each. “Which cup changed most?”
